Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `171f30f0b6a5df51e1e70b2d4c97f196bccfa9e4` on `orchestrator/project-3376` (matches integration branch metadata; no mismatch).

Clarification mapping: no `Q<ID>` items were asked for this issue; `/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]` only confirms continuation.

Actions taken: reviewed item 5 in `docs/plans/open-agents-learnings-plan.md:344-361` and the current prompt sections in `prompts/mode-implement.txt:23-29, 48-76` and `prompts/mode-implement-repair.txt:12-20`.

Assumptions made: keep the change strictly additive inside the two listed prompt files; preserve `# tier: DEFAULT` and all existing placeholders/frontmatter.

Missing-context notes: no dedicated prompt-lint command was inspected in this targeted read, so verification should rely on scoped diff review plus any existing CI that already consumes these prompt templates.

1. Files likely to change
- `prompts/mode-implement.txt`
  - Add three guardrail bullets in the early instruction area, most likely adjacent to the existing exploration/scope guidance (`23-29`, `48-76`), without rewriting existing items.
- `prompts/mode-implement-repair.txt`
  - Add repair-safe guardrail bullets near the existing minimal-edit / plan-divergence guidance (`12-20`).
- No other files should change. Do not edit `docs/plans/open-agents-learnings-plan.md` or bundle any other prompt-plan items.

2. Functions or modules to implement
- No executable code changes; this is a prompt-template update only.
- `prompts/mode-implement.txt`
  - Add bullets covering:
    - read each file completely before the first `apply_patch` on that file, using the exploration log as the checklist;
    - run independent operations in parallel and serialize only when there is an explicit dependency;
    - never make surprise edits affecting more than three files outside the plan’s `files_touched` set without flagging the expansion in the post-implementation summary.
- `prompts/mode-implement-repair.txt`
  - Add the repair variants:
    - always re-read the failing file before patching;
    - keep repairs free of surprise scope expansion / stay inside the allow-list and surface any scope drift instead of silently expanding it.
  - Do not add the parallel bullet to the repair prompt; item 5 explicitly drops it for repair turns.

3. Data structures affected
- Prompt text only:
  - `# tier: DEFAULT` frontmatter stays unchanged.
  - Existing placeholders such as `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}`, `{{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION}}`, and `{{REFERENCE_*}}` stay intact.
- No runtime data structures, schemas, contracts, or workflow metadata change.

4. API or interface changes
- No external API, CLI, or workflow interface changes.
- Internal prompt-behavior change only: implement and implement-repair phases will receive stricter edit-discipline instructions.

5. Potential risks or edge cases
- The new bullets must be additive and must not weaken the existing stronger scope rules around `files_touched` / allow-listed edits.
- Avoid contradicting the existing exploration-log guidance already in `prompts/mode-implement.txt`; this change should tighten it from “listed in exploration log” to “fully read before first patch.”
- The implement prompt’s parallelization bullet must clearly apply only to independent operations.
- The repair prompt should not accidentally inherit the implement prompt’s parallel rule.
- Preserve frontmatter and placeholders exactly.
- No factual issue/codebase conflicts found. The current prompts already contain exploration-log and scope-discipline language, so this is a local refinement, not a rewrite.

6. Testing considerations
- Verify via scoped diff that only:
  - `prompts/mode-implement.txt`
  - `prompts/mode-implement-repair.txt`
  changed.
- Confirm exact presence of:
  - all three new implement guardrails;
  - both repair-safe variants.
- Confirm `# tier: DEFAULT` and placeholders are unchanged.
- Let any existing CI/prompt-consumer checks run unchanged; do not add new validation commands just for this PR.
- Confirm no other “open agents learnings” prompt items were bundled.

7. Pre-execution self-check result
- Scope check: pass — issue scope and `files_touched` both limit the change to the two prompt files.
- Ref check: pass — checkout ref matches integration branch metadata.
- Feasibility check: pass — both target files exist, item 5 matches the requested change, and no external inputs are required.
